first_to_score_event.reviewer: independent-reviewer-SOCCER (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
first_to_score_event.rederivation_notes: Own chain, written before opening the record: (1) team scoring intensities lambda_A, lambda_B for this match from opponent-adjusted attack/defence strength, venue (club ground vs neutral), confirmed XI and keeper/striker absences; (2) a competing-risk race: the first goal is the earlier arrival of two inhomogeneous Poisson streams, so P(A first) = integral lambda_A(t) exp(-integral(lambda_A+lambda_B)) dt, with the early-minute hazard shape, set-piece and penalty routes and own-goal credit shifting it away from the plain lambda share; (3) the no-goal leg is P(0-0) over the exposure window, so low-score dependence (Dixon-Coles) and the window length decide it; the window is 90+stoppage in leagues and 120 only where the competition plays extra time (second-leg aggregate state and knockout caution then change both hazards); (4) settlement: entire game incl. extra time, shootout excluded, own goal to team awarded, a listed No Goal outcome, abandonment/postponement unknown. Required inputs: strength ratings, venue, XI/availability, first-goal hazard, route mix, penalty/referee rate, DC rho, ET rate, aggregate state, cagey factor, rules text, plus consistency with the joint goal model. Compared with the record the chain and stages s1-s4 match. Differences found: the record asserts competition-by-competition extra-time rules (UEFA Super Cup) that I believe are wrong and nowhere sourced; the merged catalog entry still carries Method-tree text on a primary input and a draw-rate interaction; the record still defines retired/detached Method inputs; several audited-WEAK inputs remain attached. Quotes: 5 rules_evidence quotes checked as substrings of market_universe/contract_rules_sample.json (all verbatim); 32 live series, 23 with rules text, 9 TITLE_ONLY (confirmed against the ledger). Kalshi series API reachable (settlement_sources, contract_terms_url, important_info); contract_terms PDFs on assets.kalshi.com returned 403 so abandonment wording remains unread.

findings.text: Wrong/unsupported competition rule used to size the race window: stage s3 and variants_and_edge_cases state that the UEFA Super Cup goes straight to penalties after 90 minutes 'under current rules' (and the contract section asserts 'German, English and UEFA super cups go to penalties without extra time'). The UEFA Super Cup is played with 2x15 extra time before penalties (e.g. the 2013, 2019, 2020 and 2023 editions were decided after extra time; reviewer knowledge, UEFA regulations could not be fetched from this container). KXUEFASCFTTS is a live rules-text series in this key and its own Kalshi important_info says extra time played is counted. The record therefore sets P(ET) = 0 for a series where it is positive, biasing P(no goal) and the 91-120 hazard need.

Per-competition extra-time/penalties rules (EFL Cup before the final, Community Shield, DFL-Supercup, Leagues Cup, Spanish/Italian/French super cups, FA Cup proper rounds after replay abolition, Copa del Rey, Coppa Italia, Liga MX liguilla, MLS playoffs) are stated as facts in s3/variants with at most a '(to be confirmed per edition)' hedge and no source; no required_data row captures 'extra time played (rule)' per competition-season from an official regulation. Needed: a regulation table per competition-season (competition rule pages) before any series is assigned exposure 90 vs 120.

Stale Method content remains in the merged catalog first_to_score_event entry although the record says it was cleaned: (a) input soc.knockout_cagey_factor is attached with role 'primary' and why 'Directly sets the gate P(draw at 90) of the method path tree' (a Method-of-Victory quantity; for FTTS it only scales both hazards in cup ties and is not primary for the 23+ league/neutral series); (b) the catalog interaction [soc.knockout_cagey_factor, soc.second_leg_aggregate_state] carries the old draw-rate hypothesis and how_to_test ('compare draw rates against a first-leg baseline'), not the FTTS wording written in the record (first-scorer share and no-goal mass); (c) category_coverage.environment note still says 'for the method tree the venue's effect ...'. The two named Method interactions were dropped, but the entry still files a Method driver as primary.

Leftover references to departed series: new_inputs still defines soc.winning_margin_distribution (a retired audited duplicate, league MOV reading) and soc.method_path_tree_calibration (detached from this key), and soc.knockout_cagey_factor's rationale talks about 'ET/penalty mass that Method contracts sell'; unresolved entries mov_mof_semantics, mov_league_outcome_set and shootout_sample_size only say the matter moved elsewhere, and archetype_mismatch is listed as an open 'unresolved' while declaring itself resolved. Stage s2 still points to 'the extra-time stage' (now s3) and duplicates the s3 window/formula text.

Audited-WEAK/duplicate inputs remain attached and category_coverage is internally inconsistent: soc.pace_press (WEAK), soc.shots (WEAK) and soc.xg (DUPLICATE_OF soc.xg_adjusted_ratings) are still in the input list and the catalog still carries the pace_press x first_goal_hazard interaction, while pace_volume is declared NOT_APPLICABLE; soc.first_goal_hazard is primary yet its catalog pregame_knowable is 'no' (the fitted pre-match parameters are knowable).

Settlement-source and template details not reflected: Kalshi series metadata (fetched 2026-11-09) names ESPN as settlement source (FIFA for KXUEFASCFTTS) and shows two contract templates inside this key (SOCCERTEAMTOSCOREFIRST for KXUCLFTTS vs SOCCERWHOSTAT for KXUEFASCFTTS, whose important_info limits extra time to 'Knockout Stage matches'); the record says 'official match report' and 'identical wording across leagues ... super cups'. Contract PDFs (abandonment clause) were not readable (HTTP 403).

soc.goal_dist (joint goal-count model) is not carried although the no-goal leg must equal the joint 0-0 cell used by the sibling match-result/total/BTTS prices; consistency is left to soc.dixon_coles_low_score alone. environment is declared NOT_APPLICABLE with stale 'method tree' wording although altitude/heat (Liga MX, AFC, AFCON qualifiers) can move early-goal hazard.

unreg:knockout_method_of_victory.reviewer: independent-reviewer-SOCCER (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:knockout_method_of_victory.rederivation_notes: Own chain, written before opening the record: the contract settles on which phase ends a knockout tie (Regular Time = 90 + stoppage, Extra Time before any shootout, Penalty Shootout), either-team (MOF) or named-team (MOV). Stages: (1) regulation scoring rates from opponent-adjusted strength, venue (neutral final, de facto home, club ground in early rounds), XI/injuries; (2) P(level after 90) = diagonal of the joint score grid (goal-count distribution with low-score dependence plus knockout caution); (3) tie structure: single match vs second leg where the aggregate, not the score, must be level and sets each side's risk posture, and competitions that skip extra time; (4) extra time: 30 minutes at a reduced, fatigue- and bench-dependent rate; (5) shootout near 50/50, small keeper/taker effects; (6) settlement: phase boundaries, fair price after cancellation beyond two weeks, source of truth; (7) scope: 37 of 41 series have no listed market, six are league names. Required inputs: ratings, joint goal distribution, cagey factor, ET rate, aggregate/tie tree, bench/load/rest, weather, shootout skill, keeper, rules flags. Compared with the record: s1-s7 broadly match; differences are that the joint goal distribution (the object behind the level cell) is attached only as context for a speculative league stage, a catalog-DUPLICATE tie tree is attached as primary, the record's scope text is still final-centred, and primary Kalshi series metadata contradicts or fills several 'unknown' statements. Quotes: all 6 rules_evidence quotes verified as substrings of KXUCLMOF/KXWCMOF/KXUELMOV/KXWCMOV samples; 41 series (4 RULES_TEXT, 37 TITLE_ONLY) confirmed in the ledger. Kalshi series API reachable; contract-terms PDFs (403) and Sports Reference/FBref (proxy refused) not reachable.

findings.text: soc.tie_advancement_state_tree is attached as PRIMARY (and drives stage s6 and a stage-pair interaction) although the catalog input audit flags it DUPLICATE_OF soc.second_leg_aggregate_state ('second-leg advancement given aggregate and tie rules ... placeholders +20%/-10%, not estimated'). The record audits it KEEP_PRIMARY without rebutting the flag, while the same duplicate standard retired soc.winning_margin_distribution. The interaction [tie tree x second_leg_aggregate_state] pairs an input with its flagged duplicate, so it is not an independent interaction. Either retire/merge one of them or document what the tree adds beyond the aggregate state (single-leg rule table, ET-vs-pens branch by competition) and demote the other.

The core regulation-level probability is the diagonal of the joint score grid (s2 says so), i.e. the object of soc.goal_dist, yet soc.goal_dist is attached only as 'context' for stage s7, a placeholder for league MOV series that may not exist; it is absent from s1/s2, from the 'input hierarchy' paragraph and from the draw-mass chain, which names cagey factor, Dixon-Coles and late appetite instead. After the DUPLICATE-substitution the surviving input should own the grid in s1/s2 (with Dixon-Coles as its correction), otherwise the structural chain has no joint distribution.

Primary metadata available but unused: Kalshi series API (fetched 2026-11-09) shows KXLALIGAMOV, KXLIGAMXMOV and KXBRASILEIROMOV (league series) and KXCOPADELREYMOV, KXUEFASCMOV, KXFACUPMOV use contract_terms SOCCERADVANCEMETHOD, the same template id as KXWCMOV (Regulation/Extra Time/Penalty legs), and KXEFLCUPMOF uses SOCCERFINISHMETHOD like KXUCLMOF; settlement_sources name ESPN (plus FIFA for World Cup/EFL Cup MOF). The record says no source of truth is named, the outcome set of the six league MOV series is unknown, and offers a regulation-margin partition (s7) as a live alternative; the template ids make the three-phase reading the better-supported one but the PDFs (assets.kalshi.com, HTTP 403 from here) must be read to confirm. u3/settlement_data_source should cite this evidence.

Required-data mapping: soc.goal_dist is listed as fed by 'Domestic-cup and super-cup tie results', whose only goal field is 'final goal difference'; a joint goal-count fit needs per-match goals_h/goals_a history (football-data.co.uk league CSVs or the strength dataset), which no dataset here supplies to it. The feed was moved from the retired input without checking this.

Interactions: [soc.penalty_shootout_skill x soc.extra_time_shootout_model] is self-described as a 'structural gate rather than a learned interaction' and the catalog measurement of the second input already builds shootout win probability from taker/keeper records (component x container, not an interaction); [soc.dixon_coles_low_score x soc.neutral_final_venue_split] attributes the effect to rho although draws rise as the expected goal gap shrinks irrespective of rho.

Stale final-centred scope text after widening to 41 series (37 unlisted cup/league series): catalog mechanism says 'A single-match knockout final', summary and s1 are written for 'two finalists' at a neutral venue; the merged catalog entry carries three interaction pairs twice (old hypothesis-only copies plus the new formed ones). Unsourced baselines presented as typical (level after 90 'about 25-35%' in the summary vs 0.2-0.4 in s2; ET goals 0.5-0.8; P(level at 120) 0.5-0.6).

competition_winner_and_top_n.reviewer: independent-reviewer-SOCCER (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
competition_winner_and_top_n.rederivation_notes: Own chain, written before opening the record: an outright is a sum over scenarios of latent team strength, remaining schedule and format. (1) strength with drift and a preseason prior, posterior width mattering for the maximum of several totals; (2) Monte Carlo of remaining fixtures through a joint goal model into sampled tables, with tiebreaks and schedule asymmetry; (3) format conversion: split-season, playoff, liguilla, bracket with extra time and penalties, group-plus-bracket tournaments and the 36-team UEFA league phase; (4) multi-competition load and rotation, injuries, transfers, manager changes; (5) rank thresholds and the density near the cut line for top-N, qualification slot allocation; (6) joint placings for unions, exact orders and group outcomes; (7) administrative shocks (deductions, voided seasons) and the exact competition-season definition; (8) single-match residuals priced with the match model. Required inputs: ratings and uncertainty, preseason prior, comp_sim, schedule strength, tiebreakers, format conversion, bracket path, joint finish distribution, load/depth/injuries/transfers, deductions, slot allocation, rules text. Compared with the record: s1-s8 match my chain. Differences found: market-derived m.external_lines remains PRIMARY in the catalog although audited BENCHMARK_ONLY; soc.european_slot_spillover is attached despite a DUPLICATE flag; the KXWCWINMARGIN 'final margin' premise of s8 is unsupported; goal_dist/ET-model feeds sit in a structure dataset without goals. Quotes: all 8 rules_evidence quotes verified as substrings of the samples; counts 110 live series, 99 RULES_TEXT, 11 TITLE_ONLY confirmed against the ledger; KXWCWINMARGIN, KXAFCCL2GAME and KXWCFINALMATCHUP are NO_MARKETS_LISTED in the sample.

findings.text: Market-derived input kept as a primary input: catalog competition_winner_and_top_n lists m.external_lines with role 'primary' (and m.ladder_structure 'secondary') although the record audits both BENCHMARK_ONLY; no archetype patch demotes or detaches them, so the catalog still presents a bookmaker price as a primary driver while the record says it is a benchmark. Roles must be patched (or the inputs detached) so benchmarks are not inputs.

KXWCWINMARGIN is treated as 'the final's winning margin' (s8 text, soc.goal_dist attach reason, input_audit reason) but the only evidence is the title 'World Cup Winning Margin', status NO_MARKETS_LISTED, and Kalshi series metadata scope 'Winning Margin' (terms SOCCERWINMARGIN; fetched 2026-11-09); sibling KX*WINMARGIN series in other sports are per-game margin-bucket markets (e.g. KXNBAWINMARGIN-...-BKN6TO10). If it is per match across the tournament it is a match-margin contract misfiled in the outright key, and s8's regulation/ET/shootout framing and the goal_dist role are built on an unverified premise. The variants line says 'plausibly' but s8 and the audit state it as fact, and it is not in series_mapping_issues or unresolved as SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.

soc.european_slot_spillover is attached (context) and staged in s5, but the catalog input audit flags it DUPLICATE_OF soc.tiebreaker_rules ('slot allocation ... already inside soc.tiebreaker_rules; context only until a qualification-based series exists'). The reconcile pass added a KEEP_CONTEXT audit for it without rebutting that flag, while the same standard retired soc.winning_margin_distribution. KXEPLTOP4's qualification wording is real, but then the input needs a distinct measurement (slot count distribution) and the duplicate flag must be answered or the input retired.

Data mapping for the s8 residuals: soc.goal_dist (and soc.extra_time_shootout_model, home_advantage) are listed as fed by 'Tournament structure and set definitions for joint simulation', whose fields contain no goals; match goals (goals_h, goals_a) sit in the fixtures dataset whose feeds_inputs omit goal_dist. soc.extra_time_shootout_model, used in s8, is carried by the season_outcome blueprint but has no input_audit entry in this record.

Audit/catalog divergence: stage s1 lists soc.xg as an input though it is audited WEAK ('used only through ratings'); soc.xg and soc.top_two_order_statistics (audited IRRELEVANT) and m.external_lines/m.ladder_structure stay attached and unused by any stage or interaction; coverage efficiency note says soc.xg is not cited as cover but s1 still cites it.

Two filed-elsewhere series remain here: KXWCFINALMATCHUP (bracket composition) and KXAFCCL2GAME (match result) are listed in series_mapping_issues but still counted in the 110 live series and priced by stage s7/s8 on guesses; the record labels them TITLE_ONLY whereas the sample shows NO_MARKETS_LISTED (no title text at all).
